description: Secrets. `detect`: SecretPatterns.match (which pattern makes text look like a secret: private-key, token, jwt, url-password anywhere in it; card-number, generated-password, random for the whole trimmed text; null for none). `reasons`: ClipboardSecrets.reason (marked by the app, then a password manager, then the look when `patterns` is on). `passwordManagers`: PasswordManagers.contains (case-insensitive). `names`: the name a sensitive hotstring's secret gets from its trigger, unique among `taken`. `sessions`: the Sensitive switch and its helpers on a configuration's hotstrings and secrets (an index out of range does nothing), with config.json and secrets.json as Swift writes them, each hotstring's text (null while its secret is missing), `missing`, and the names in use. `keys`: a secret's config key (`secrets.json › name`; the path keeps `secrets.`). Hotstring ids are fixed.

sessions.name: on and off: the text moves to secrets.json under a name from the trigger, and back
a missing secret: no text until it's entered; off brings back an empty replacement
duplicates get their own secret; a secret goes when no hotstring uses it
names: a sensitive hotstring's name is taken even while its text is missing
